sense: a class or group in a classification

evidence: Plin. Ep. 2.6.2: in tria genera discrīpserat
terms.comment: The general word for a class of things or people, its commonest sense in every period (Lewis & Short). Also birth, descent, a race or family, and in grammar gender. In genera dīvidere, discrībere: to sort into categories. For “kind, sort” in everyday talk, see kind.
Classically one of the Servian property classes of citizens, and the fleet; figuratively a rank (philosophers “of the fifth class”, Cic.). Not a general word for a category of things.
Greek κατηγορία: post-classical, and only in logic (the pure Latin is praedicāmenta); also an accusation (Jerome).

phrases.latin: Vīnum etiam parvolīs lagunculīs in tria genera discrīpserat, nōn ut potestās ēligendī, sed nē jūs esset recūsandī
phrases.english: He had even sorted the wine, in little flasks, into three categories, not so that one could choose but so that one had no right to refuse

sources: Lewis & Short: genus · Lewis & Short: classis · Lewis & Short: categoria
